title: Eloralintide (LY3841136): Selective Amylin Receptor Agonist — Phase 2 Lancet Data & Phase 3 Launch
excerpt: Eloralintide (LY3841136) is Eli Lilly's once-weekly selective amylin receptor agonist with Lancet Phase 2 data showing up to 20.1% weight loss at 48 weeks — a novel non-GLP-1 obesity peptide now in Phase 3 ENLIGHTEN trials.
content:
Research Disclaimer: Eloralintide (LY3841136) is an investigational compound. It is not approved by the FDA or any regulatory agency as of November 2026. Content is for educational and research purposes only. Not medical advice. Consult a qualified healthcare provider before making any health decisions.

What Is Eloralintide?

Eloralintide (development code: LY3841136) is a novel once-weekly selective amylin receptor agonist developed by Eli Lilly and Company for the treatment of obesity and overweight. It represents a genuinely distinct mechanistic class within the obesity pharmacotherapy landscape — one that does not rely on GLP-1 receptor activation for its effects.

Amylin is a 37-amino-acid peptide co-secreted with insulin from pancreatic beta cells in response to meals. It acts via calcitonin receptor (CTR) and calcitonin receptor-like receptor (CLR) complexes in the brainstem's area postrema and hypothalamus to reduce food intake, suppress post-meal glucagon secretion, and slow gastric emptying. Pramlintide (Symlin), an earlier amylin analog, was FDA-approved in 2005 but required multiple daily injections and had limited commercial adoption. Eloralintide's engineering for once-weekly dosing overcomes this barrier.

Phase 2 data, published in The Lancet (November 2025), showed up to 20.1% weight loss at 48 weeks. Phase 3 ENLIGHTEN trials began enrolling in 2026.

How Eloralintide Differs From Amycretin

This is the most common point of confusion. Both involve amylin receptor signaling, but the approach is fundamentally different:

Eloralintide's selectivity for amylin receptors makes it a candidate for add-on therapy in people who have maximized benefit from GLP-1 agonists but have not achieved target weight loss — a scenario the ENLIGHTEN-6 trial is designed to study.

Mechanism of Action

Amylin Receptor Activation

  • Binds calcitonin receptor (CTR) and calcitonin receptor-like receptor (CLR) complexes — the native amylin receptors
  • Acts primarily in the brainstem's area postrema and the hypothalamic arcuate nucleus
  • Reduces meal size and meal frequency (satiety signaling independent of GLP-1 pathway)
  • Suppresses post-prandial glucagon secretion, limiting hepatic glucose output after meals
  • Slows gastric emptying by a mechanism distinct from, and possibly additive to, GLP-1-mediated gastric slowing

Why Non-GLP-1 Matters

GLP-1 pathway saturation is a practical concern in the clinic: some patients on high-dose semaglutide or tirzepatide continue to have significant hunger and suboptimal weight loss. Adding a mechanistically distinct satiety signal — via amylin receptors — could provide incremental benefit without redosing the GLP-1 pathway. The ENLIGHTEN-6 and the planned EloraTZP (eloralintide + tirzepatide) combination trials test this hypothesis directly.

Key Research Findings

Phase 2 — Published in The Lancet (November 2025)

Design: 48-week, multicentre, double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial in 263 adults with obesity or overweight without type 2 diabetes.

Key observations:

  • Weight loss had not plateaued by 48 weeks at the highest dose, indicating continued potential

Dosing in Research

Note: The following reflects clinical trial protocols only. Eloralintide is not approved or commercially available.

  • Route: Subcutaneous injection (once weekly)
  • Dose range studied in Phase 2: Multiple ascending doses with highest dose achieving 20.1% weight loss
  • Duration: 48 weeks in Phase 2; longer in Phase 3
  • Titration: Dose escalation protocol to minimize nausea

Frequently Asked Questions

What makes eloralintide different from amycretin, which also involves amylin?

Both involve amylin receptor signaling, but the mechanism and molecular strategy differ fundamentally. Amycretin (Novo Nordisk, NN9487) is a dual GLP-1 and amylin agonist — a single molecule that simultaneously activates both receptor systems. Eloralintide (LY3841136) is a selective amylin receptor agonist only — it has no GLP-1 activity. This means eloralintide could in principle be combined with GLP-1 drugs (or GLP-1/GIP drugs like tirzepatide) to add amylin pathway satiety on top of existing GLP-1 treatment. The ENLIGHTEN-6 trial specifically studies eloralintide in people already on weekly incretin therapy, and an EloraTZP co-formulation with tirzepatide is planned. Phase 2 Lancet data (2025) showed up to 20.1% weight loss at 48 weeks.

Why hasn't an amylin-only drug been developed before eloralintide?

Pramlintide (Symlin), an injectable amylin analog, was FDA-approved in 2005 for diabetes but required multiple daily injections, limiting adoption for obesity. Eloralintide is engineered for once-weekly dosing by incorporating half-life extension technologies, solving the compliance problem that limited pramlintide. Synthetic amylin analogs also require careful balancing of receptor selectivity at CTR and CLR complexes to optimize efficacy while managing side effects like nausea. Lilly's Phase 2 data published in The Lancet (2025) suggests the once-weekly approach achieves 20% weight loss without the dosing burden, representing a meaningful technical advance over earlier amylin approaches.

What is the current status of eloralintide and can I enroll in a trial?

Eloralintide is fully investigational — not FDA-approved and not commercially available as of November 2026. Multiple Phase 3 ENLIGHTEN trials are actively recruiting. To check eligibility and enrollment sites, visit ClinicalTrials.gov — ENLIGHTEN-1 (NCT07321886). Participation in clinical research is the only legal access to eloralintide at this time.

Research Limitations and Open Questions

  • Phase 3 ENLIGHTEN results not yet available (expected 2027–2028)
  • No published data in diabetic obesity population yet (ENLIGHTEN-2 ongoing)
  • Comparative efficacy vs. semaglutide, tirzepatide, amycretin not from head-to-head trials
  • Cardiac effects of amylin receptor agonism (CTR is expressed in cardiac tissue) under continued study
  • Long-term durability and weight regain after discontinuation not established
  • Combination EloraTZP data not yet available
